dc21.title: Activity feed: Load more
dc21.summary: A deploy dashboard's activity feed already shows page 1. Add Load more: fetch the next page and append it until there are none left.
dc21.brief:
Shipyard is a deploy dashboard. App.tsx has Sidebar, StatCard and an ActivityFeed card that already loads and shows the first page (read its effect). Your job is paging.

Read api.ts: getActivity(page) returns { items, nextPage }, where nextPage is null on the last page. The starter ignores nextPage. Each call takes a random 0.5–1.2 s. There are 13 events, 5 per page.

The button and the end line are already styled in styles.css (.feed-footer, .load-more, .feed-end), so this one is all React.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4.

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–3 plan · 3–11 Core · 11–15 Next

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"items and loading already live in ActivityFeed. I add nextPage next to them and set it from the first response too, because the API tells me the next page and I don't want to count pages myself. Load more fetches nextPage and appends with setItems((prev) => [...prev, ...page.items]). The button only renders while nextPage !== null; it says Loading… and is disabled while a request is in flight, which also stops double clicks from fetching the same page twice."
requirements: Store the nextPage that getActivity returns (the starter throws it away). While there is a next page, a Load more button (.load-more inside .feed-footer) shows under the list
Clicking it fetches nextPage and appends those rows: the first 5 stay, now 10 rows. Use the updater form of setItems
While a page loads the button reads Loading… and is disabled. Rapid double clicks never load the same page twice
After the last page (13 rows) the button disappears and a muted line reads "You're all caught up · 13 events" (.feed-end)
hints: The starter calls getActivity(1) but only keeps page.items. What else is in that response that you need later?
One more piece of state: const [nextPage, setNextPage] = useState<number | null>(null); Set it in the existing effect and after every Load more.
Appending must use the updater form, because the old list is what you add to: setItems((prev) => { return [...prev, ...page.items]; });
Search: "react disable button while loading". Disabled buttons don't fire onClick, which is your double-click guard. Add an early if (loading || nextPage === null) { return; } too.

Shape: let footer = null; if (items.length > 0 && nextPage !== null) { footer = <div className="feed-footer"><button ...>{label}</button></div>; } else if (items.length > 0) { footer = <p className="feed-end">…</p>; }
rubric: Read the existing effect first and extended it instead of rewriting it
Stored nextPage from the API instead of computing pages by hand
Appends with the updater form; never mutates or replaces the list
Reused ActivityItem and the existing classes
Button label/disabled derived from loading; no duplicate requests
End state handled (button removed, caught-up line)

primitives.name: Spread to append
primitives.example:
const a = [1, 2];
const b = [...a, ...[3, 4]];   // [1, 2, 3, 4]  (a is unchanged)
primitives.note: Returns a new array with both lists inside. Never push into state: React needs a new array to notice the change.

primitives.name: useState updater form
primitives.example: setCount((c) => { return c + 1; });   // uses the latest value, not the one from this render
primitives.note: Pass a function when the new state depends on the old one. React calls it with the current value and stores what you return.

primitives.name: Nullable state
primitives.example:
const [nextPage, setNextPage] = useState<number | null>(null);
if (nextPage === null) { /* no more pages */ }
primitives.note: number | null means "a number, or nothing yet". TypeScript then makes you check !== null before using it as a number.

primitives.name: Disabled button
primitives.example: <button disabled={true} onClick={go}>Load more</button>   // click does nothing
primitives.note: A disabled button never fires onClick, so it doubles as a guard against double clicks. Style it with :disabled.

dc22.title: Blog editor: tag input
dc22.summary: Turn the plain Tags field of a blog editor into a chip input: Enter or comma adds, Backspace removes, no duplicates, max 5.
dc22.brief:
Inkwell is a blogging editor. App.tsx has TopBar, Editor, PostSettings and a TagField that is just a text input for now. The post (App) already owns tags and passes tags + onChange down to TagField, which ignores them.

Read utils/tags.ts (cleanTag and MAX_TAGS) and components/Chip.tsx (a chip that shows a × when you pass onRemove). Both are meant to be reused. The red error style .field-help.is-error is already in styles.css. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (5 is a stretch).

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–4 plan · 4–14 Core · 14–20 Next

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The tags belong to the post, so they stay in App; TagField never copies them into its own state, it calls onChange with a new array. The half-typed text and the error message are local to TagField. Everything happens in one onKeyDown: Enter or comma calls addTag (with preventDefault so the comma isn't typed), and Backspace on an empty draft drops the last tag. addTag cleans the text, ignores empty, then later checks duplicates with some on lowercase and the max."
requirements: Typing a tag and pressing Enter or , adds it as a <Chip> inside the box, before the input, and clears the input. The comma is never typed. Text is cleaned with cleanTag; empty tags are ignored. Add by calling onChange with a new array (the tags live in App)
Each chip's × removes that tag (pass onRemove to Chip)
Backspace in an empty input removes the last chip
Duplicates are ignored case-insensitively ("React" then "react" adds one chip) and the help line shows "react" is already added. in red (.field-help.is-error)
At 5 tags, adding another shows You can add up to 5 tags. and does not add it. Normally the help line reads "Press Enter or comma to add · 2 / 5"
hints: tags already lives in App and arrives as a prop. You never change it directly: call onChange([...tags, tag]).
Search: "mdn keydown event key". e.key is "Enter", "," or "Backspace".
Search: "react onKeyDown preventDefault". Without e.preventDefault() the comma lands in the input.
Remove one: onChange(tags.filter((t) => { return t !== tag; })); Duplicates: tags.some((t) => { return t.toLowerCase() === tag.toLowerCase(); })

Shape: function handleKeyDown(e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) { if (e.key === "Enter" || e.key === ",") { e.preventDefault(); addTag(); return; } if (e.key === "Backspace" && draft === "" && tags.length > 0) { onChange(tags.slice(0, -1)); } }
rubric: Used the tags/onChange props; didn't copy tags into local state
One onKeyDown handler; preventDefault for Enter/comma
Reused cleanTag, MAX_TAGS and Chip
Case-insensitive duplicate check with some()
New arrays only (spread, filter, slice); no push/splice on state
Message state cleared on success; help line derived

primitives.name: e.key
primitives.example:
// onKeyDown on an input
e.key   // 'Enter', ',', 'Backspace', 'a', 'ArrowLeft'…
primitives.note: The name of the key that was pressed, as a string. Use onKeyDown (not onChange) to react to Enter or Backspace.

primitives.name: e.preventDefault()
primitives.note: Stops the browser's default action for this event (typing the character, submitting a form, following a link). Returns nothing.

primitives.name: filter() to remove
primitives.note: Returns a new array with only the items where your function returned true. The original is unchanged: perfect for removing from state.

primitives.name: some() + case-insensitive compare
primitives.example: ['React', 'CSS'].some((t) => { return t.toLowerCase() === 'react'; })   // true
primitives.note: Returns true as soon as one item matches, else false. Lower-case both sides so "React" and "react" count as the same.

dc23.title: Pomodoro timer
dc23.summary: Make a focus timer actually tick: Start/Pause, Reset, mm:ss, and an automatic 5-minute break at 00:00, with exactly one interval.
dc23.brief:
Ripe is a focus app. App.tsx has Header, Timer (static 25:00 with Start/Reset buttons that do nothing), SessionDots and a TaskList from components/.

Read utils/time.ts: formatTime(seconds) gives "mm:ss", and FOCUS_SECONDS / BREAK_SECONDS are already defined. The Break look (.timer.mode-break) and the progress bar (.progress, .progress-fill) are already styled in styles.css. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (5 is a stretch).

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–4 plan · 4–14 Core · 14–20 Next

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"I store secondsLeft and running in Timer (and later mode). The display is formatTime(secondsLeft), never a stored string. One effect depends on running: if running, it starts setInterval and the cleanup clears it, so pausing, resetting or unmounting always kills it and there's never a second one. The tick uses setSecondsLeft((s) => s - 1) because the interval closure would see a stale value. For the break, a second effect watches for 0 and switches mode, and the finished-session count goes up to App through an onFocusComplete callback, because SessionDots needs it."
requirements: Start counts down once per second from 25:00 in mm:ss (24:59, 24:58…) using formatTime. While running the button reads Pause; Pause stops it, Start resumes from the same time
Exactly one interval ever runs: clicking Start/Pause quickly many times never makes it tick faster, and the interval is cleared on pause and unmount (effect cleanup)
Reset stops the timer and returns to Focus 25:00

At 00:00 the timer switches to Break at 05:00 and keeps running (pill reads "Break", .timer gets mode-break). When the break hits 00:00 it returns to Focus 25:00 and stops. Each completed focus session fills one dot: "1 of 4 sessions"
The progress bar (.progress > .progress-fill) under the time fills as the current session runs, derived from secondsLeft
hints: What has to be state? Seconds left, running or not, focus or break. The "mm:ss" text is derived.
Search: "react setInterval useEffect cleanup". The effect depends on [running]; return () => { clearInterval(id); }.
Inside setInterval, secondsLeft is frozen at the value from when the effect ran. Use setSecondsLeft((s) => { return s - 1; });
Switching at zero: a second effect on [secondsLeft, mode]: if (secondsLeft > 0) { return; } if (mode === "focus") { setMode("break"); setSecondsLeft(BREAK_SECONDS); onFocusComplete(); } else { ... }
Shape: useEffect(() => { if (!running) { return; } const id = setInterval(() => { setSecondsLeft((s) => { return s - 1; }); }, 1000); return () => { clearInterval(id); }; }, [running]);
rubric: Interval lives in an effect keyed on running, with clearInterval cleanup
Tick uses the updater form (no stale closure)
Display derived with the existing formatTime helper
Mode switch at zero handled once, cleanly
Session count lifted to App through a callback
Explained why double intervals can't happen

notes: pill, border, button and bar turn leaf green

primitives.name: setInterval / clearInterval
primitives.example:
const id = setInterval(() => { console.log('tick'); }, 1000);   // every second
clearInterval(id);   // stops it
primitives.note: setInterval returns an id. Keep it: the only way to stop the interval is clearInterval(id).

primitives.name: useEffect cleanup
primitives.note: The function you return runs before the effect runs again (deps changed) and when the component unmounts. That is what guarantees one interval.

primitives.name: Stale closure in an interval
primitives.example:
// ✗ setSeconds(seconds - 1)   -> 'seconds' is frozen at the value from when the effect ran
// ✓ setSeconds((s) => { return s - 1; })   // always the latest value
primitives.note: Callbacks created once (intervals, listeners) keep seeing the state from that render. The updater form avoids it.

dc24.title: Dashboard theme switcher
dc24.summary: Add Light / Dark / System to an analytics dashboard with CSS variables on a data-theme attribute, remembered in localStorage.
dc24.brief:
Northwind Metrics is a SaaS dashboard: KPI cards, a revenue chart and an invoice table. Every color in styles.css comes from variables on :root, and the bottom of the file already has a dark palette under .app[data-theme="dark"]: nothing uses it yet.

Read components/SegmentedControl.tsx: the date-range switch already uses it, and the theme switch should too. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3 (4 is a stretch).

Timeline: 0–2 read · 2–4 plan · 4–15 Core · 15–20 Next

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"I store the user's choice (light, dark or system) in App. The applied theme is derived: the choice, or the OS theme from matchMedia when the choice is system. I put it on the root div as data-theme, and the existing CSS redefines the variables, which inherit to everything inside. Then saving: lazy initial state from localStorage inside a try/catch, because storage can throw, and a save in the click handler. For live OS changes I listen to the matchMedia change event in an effect with cleanup."
requirements: A second SegmentedControl labelled "Theme" in the top bar with Light, Dark, System. The app root gets data-theme="light" or "dark", and the existing dark palette kicks in. No component changes its own colors
System uses the OS setting: window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches. The applied theme is derived from the choice, never stored separately
The choice is saved to localStorage key northwind-theme and restored on reload. Every storage read and write is wrapped in try/catch; with no saved (or an unknown) value the default is System
System follows the OS live: changing the OS setting updates the page without a reload. Next to the switch a muted note reads "Using dark" / "Using light" while System is chosen
hints: Two different things: what the user picked (3 options) and what's applied (2 options). Only the first one is state.
Read the bottom of styles.css. Variables inherit, so .app[data-theme="dark"] beats the :root values for everything inside. You only set the attribute.
Search: "mdn matchMedia". window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches is true or false.

Search: "mdn localStorage exceptions". getItem and setItem can throw (private mode, blocked storage). Wrap both. Lazy initial state reads once: useState<ThemeChoice>(() => { return readStoredChoice(); })
Live updates: const mq = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"); mq.addEventListener("change", handle); return () => { mq.removeEventListener("change", handle); };
rubric: Stored the choice; derived the applied theme
Applied the theme with one data-theme attribute (no per-component colors)
Reused SegmentedControl
localStorage wrapped in try/catch, read lazily once
Validated the stored value instead of trusting it
matchMedia listener added and removed in an effect

notes: same SegmentedControl · after date range · gap 10

primitives.name: data-* attributes
primitives.example: <div className="app" data-theme="dark">   // CSS: .app[data-theme="dark"] { --bg: #0B1120; }
primitives.note: Any data-something prop is passed straight to the DOM. CSS can select on it with [data-theme="dark"].
primitives.search: mdn data attributes css attribute selector

primitives.name: matchMedia().matches
primitives.example: window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches   // true if the OS is in dark mode
primitives.note: Runs a CSS media query from JS. .matches is true/false right now; the returned object also fires a change event.

primitives.name: localStorage + try/catch
primitives.note: getItem returns a string or null; it stores strings only. Both calls can throw, so wrap them.

primitives.name: Type assertion (as)
primitives.note: Tells TypeScript "trust me, this string is one of these". It does not check anything at runtime, so only use it when you know it's true.

dc25.title: Chat composer: emoji picker
dc25.summary: A team-chat composer gets an emoji popover: open it from 🙂, insert at the cursor, close on outside click or Escape.
dc25.brief:
Huddle is a team chat. App.tsx has Sidebar, the message list (using components/Message.tsx) and a working Composer: type, Send appends a message. The 🙂 button in the composer bar does nothing yet.

Read components/EmojiPicker.tsx: the contents of the popover already exist. It loads the categories from getEmojiCategories() (0.4–1.0 s) every time it mounts, shows "Loading emoji…", then tabs and an 8-column grid, and calls onPick(emoji). It doesn't know when to open or where the text is: that's your job. Its insides are styled; the popover box (position, size, shadow) is your CSS.

The hard part is inserting where the cursor is, not at the end. The textarea keeps its selection after it loses focus.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change (~16 min): a recently used row.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–16 Core · 16–20 change · 20–25 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"text lives in Composer, so pickerOpen and handlePick go there too. I render the existing EmojiPicker only while open, inside a position: relative wrapper around the button, with the popover absolutely positioned above it. For the cursor I need a ref on the textarea: read selectionStart/selectionEnd, splice the emoji into the text, close. Then the polish: a mousedown listener on document closes it when the click is outside the wrapper, a keydown listener handles Escape, both only while open; and after the re-render I put the caret after the emoji."
requirements: Clicking 🙂 toggles a popover above the button: render the existing <EmojiPicker /> only while open, inside a wrapper around the button. Write the popover CSS: .emoji-popover absolute, 40px above the button, w 296, pad 10, radius 12, shadow (see spec)
Clicking an emoji inserts it at the cursor (replacing any selected text), not at the end: with "See you" and the caret after "See", picking 😀 gives "See😀 you". Then the popover closes
The popover closes on a click outside it and on Escape. Clicking inside it (e.g. switching tabs) keeps it open. Listeners are only attached while open and are removed in the effect cleanup
After inserting, the textarea is focused with the caret right after the emoji, so typing continues there

change.title: Recently used row
change.html:
"People use the same five emoji all day. Put them at the top."

  • When at least one emoji has been picked, the popover shows a Recently used row above the tabs (EmojiPicker already renders it from its recent prop).
  • Most recent first, no duplicates (picking one again moves it to the front), at most 8.
  • It must survive the popover closing and reopening.

Hint: the picker unmounts on close, so this state can't live in it.

hints: Where does the text live? The picker only reports which emoji (onPick); the composer changes the text.
Popover CSS: the wrapper gets position: relative; .emoji-popover gets position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: 40px; so it sits above the button.
Search: "mdn HTMLTextAreaElement selectionStart". el.selectionStart and el.selectionEnd are indexes into the value. Get el from useRef<HTMLTextAreaElement>(null).
Insert: text.slice(0, start) + emoji + text.slice(end). Emoji are usually 2 UTF-16 units, so the new caret is start + emoji.length.

Outside click: put the button and popover in one wrapper with a ref, then if (wrapRef.current && !wrapRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)) { setPickerOpen(false); } in a mousedown listener. Search: "mdn setSelectionRange" for the caret.
Recent: setRecent((prev) => { return [emoji, ...prev.filter((x) => { return x !== emoji; })].slice(0, 8); }); in Composer, then <EmojiPicker recent={recent} … />.
rubric: Planned state placement (text, open, recent in Composer)
Reused EmojiPicker; mounted only while open
Used selectionStart/selectionEnd and restored the caret after render
Popover positioned with relative wrapper + absolute box
Outside click uses one wrapper ref; document listeners added only while open and cleaned up
Recent row is deduped, capped, most-recent-first, and survives close
Talked through anything unfinished

notes: w 296 · pad 10 · radius 12 · bottom 40 above button

primitives.name: useRef for a DOM element
primitives.example:
const el = textareaRef.current;   // the real <textarea>, or null before it mounts
if (el) { el.focus(); }
primitives.note: ref.current is the DOM node after render (null before). Changing a ref doesn't re-render.

primitives.name: selectionStart / selectionEnd
primitives.note: Indexes into el.value: where the selection starts and ends. Equal when it's just a caret. Kept after the textarea loses focus.

primitives.name: Insert with slice
primitives.example: 'See you'.slice(0, 3) + '😀' + 'See you'.slice(3)   // 'See😀 you'
primitives.note: slice(a, b) returns the part from index a up to (not including) b; slice(a) goes to the end. Strings never change in place.

primitives.name: Absolute inside relative
primitives.syntax: .wrap { position: relative; } .pop { position: absolute; bottom: 40px; left: 0; }
primitives.example:
.emoji-anchor { position: relative; }
.emoji-popover { position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: 40px; }   /* 40px above the wrapper's bottom edge */
primitives.note: An absolute element is placed relative to the nearest positioned ancestor. Without position: relative on the wrapper it flies to the page.

primitives.name: Move to front, dedupe, cap
primitives.note: filter drops the old copy, the spread puts it first, slice(0, 8) keeps at most 8. All return new arrays.

dc26.title: People search: debounce + races
dc26.summary: A company directory search: 300 ms debounce, loading state, and stale responses that must never overwrite newer ones.
dc26.brief:
Roster is an HR directory. App.tsx has the top bar, a SearchBox (controlled) and a PersonRow that uses components/Avatar.tsx. Typing does nothing yet.

Read api.ts carefully: searchPeople(query) is slower for shorter queries ("j" ≈ 1.3 s, "jan" ≈ 0.7 s). So if you search "j" and then "jan", the "j" answer arrives last. A naive version shows the wrong results.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4–5. Change (~19 min): highlight the match.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–19 Core · 19–24 change · 24–28 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"query is state; results and loading are state because they come from the network. One effect on [query] does everything: if the query is empty it clears results and returns. Otherwise it starts a 300 ms setTimeout that calls the API. The cleanup does two jobs: clearTimeout (that's the debounce, because every keystroke cancels the pending call) and cancelled = true (so a response from an older query is ignored when it arrives late)."
requirements: Typing searches with searchPeople, debounced 300 ms: typing "jan" quickly makes one request, not three

While a request is in flight a "Searching…" line shows under the search box; results render with <PersonRow />. Empty input (or clearing it) shows "Start typing to search 18 people." with no request and no Searching… line
Out-of-order responses never win: type "j", wait ~0.4 s, then type "an". After everything settles the list shows the 5 "jan" people, not the 7 "j" people
No matches: No people match "xyz".
Old results stay visible (dimmed) while a newer search loads, instead of flashing empty

change.title: Highlight the match
change.html:
"People scan the list for why it matched. Highlight it."

  • In each name, wrap the first case-insensitive match of the query in <mark> (teal-soft background, dark teal text). "jan" in "Ben Janssen" highlights "Jan".
  • Highlight with the query the results belong to, not the one being typed right now.

Hint: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Split the string into before / match / after.

hints: Debounce in React is just setTimeout in an effect plus clearTimeout in the cleanup.
Search: "react useEffect race condition fetch". The fix is a let cancelled = false per effect run, set to true in the cleanup.
The cleanup runs before the next effect run, so when query changes, the previous run is cancelled both ways: its timer and its response.
Highlight: const i = text.toLowerCase().indexOf(q.toLowerCase()); then text.slice(0, i), text.slice(i, i + q.length), text.slice(i + q.length).

Shape: useEffect(() => { if (q === "") { ...; return; } let cancelled = false; const t = setTimeout(() => { setLoading(true); searchPeople(q).then((data) => { if (cancelled) { return; } setResults(data); setLoading(false); }); }, 300); return () => { cancelled = true; clearTimeout(t); }; }, [query]);
rubric: Explained the race before coding it
Debounce via setTimeout + clearTimeout in cleanup
Stale responses ignored via cancelled flag
Empty query short-circuits (no request)
Loading and empty states are distinct and correct
Highlight derived by slicing, uses the results' query
Reused Avatar / PersonRow

primitives.name: Debounce with setTimeout
primitives.example:
const t = setTimeout(() => { search('jan'); }, 300);
clearTimeout(t);   // cancelled: search never runs
primitives.note: setTimeout returns an id; clearTimeout(id) cancels it if it hasn't fired yet. Cancel on every keystroke = debounce.

primitives.name: Ignore stale responses
primitives.syntax: let cancelled = false; ... return () => { cancelled = true; };
primitives.note: Each effect run gets its own flag. The cleanup flips it when the query changes, so a late answer for an old query is dropped.

primitives.name: trim()
primitives.example:
'  jan '.trim()   // 'jan'
'   '.trim() === ''   // true: treat as empty
primitives.note: Returns a new string without spaces at both ends. Use it before checking "is the box empty?".

primitives.name: indexOf() to find a match
primitives.example:
'Ben Janssen'.toLowerCase().indexOf('jan')   // 4
'Ben'.indexOf('x')   // -1 (not found)
primitives.note: Returns the index of the first match, or -1. Pair it with slice to cut before / match / after.

dc27.title: Kanban: move cards
dc27.summary: A roadmap board already loads its cards. Move them between To do / Doing / Done with arrows, count each column, add cards. Then a WIP limit.
dc27.brief:
Trellis is a project board. App.tsx has CardView, Column and a Board that already loads the cards from getCards() (0.5–1.2 s) into one flat cards array and derives each column with cardsIn(columnId). Cards can't move yet and the headers have no counts.

Read api.ts (each card has a column) and board.ts (COLUMNS in left-to-right order, and label names).

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3 (4 is a stretch). Change (~20 min): WIP limit on Doing.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–20 Core · 20–25 change · 25–30 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The single source of truth is already there: one flat cards array where each card knows its column, and columns derived with filter, so I never keep three lists in sync. The count is just .length of the filtered list. Moving is map: same card with column set to the next or previous entry in COLUMNS, found with findIndex. Column stays presentational: it gets its index (to disable the edge arrows) and an onMove callback. The add form is its own small component with its own input state."
requirements: Each column header shows a count pill (.count): To do 3, Doing 2, Done 2. Counts update as cards move

Each card has ← and → buttons that move it to the previous / next column (order from COLUMNS). ← is disabled in To do and → in Done. Cards are updated immutably by id (map + spread) in the one cards array, never three lists
Under To do, an input + Add button (a form, so Enter works) adds a card with that title to the bottom of To do and clears the input. Blank titles are ignored
Doing's count reads 2 / 3 and turns red (.count.is-full) at 3 / 3

change.title: WIP limit on Doing
change.html:
"The team keeps starting things and never finishing. Limit Doing to 3."

  • Moving a card into Doing when it already has 3 is blocked: the card stays, and a red banner above the board says Doing is at its WIP limit of 3. Finish something first.
  • Any successful move clears the banner.

Check the rule before you update state.

hints: One array or three? If each card stores its column, a move is a one-field change.
Next column: const from = COLUMNS.findIndex((c) => { return c.id === card.column; }); const target = COLUMNS[from + step]; where step is -1 or 1.
Move: setCards((prev) => { return prev.map((c) => { if (c.id !== id) { return c; } return { ...c, column: target.id }; }); });
Search: "react form onSubmit preventDefault" for the add form, so Enter submits without reloading.
WIP: check before moving: if (target.id === "doing" && cardsIn("doing").length >= WIP_LIMIT) { setNotice(...); return; }
rubric: Kept the single flat array + derived columns; no parallel state
Immutable move by id; edge arrows disabled
Column stays presentational (props + callbacks)
Add form is controlled, uses onSubmit + preventDefault, ignores blanks
WIP rule checked before the update, with clear feedback
Talked through anything unfinished

primitives.name: findIndex()
primitives.example:
COLUMNS.findIndex((c) => { return c.id === 'doing'; })   // 1
COLUMNS.findIndex((c) => { return c.id === 'nope'; })    // -1

primitives.syntax: prev.map((c) => { if (c.id !== id) { return c; } return { ...c, column: next }; })

dc28.title: Comments: inline replies
dc28.summary: On a recipe page, Reply opens one inline box under that comment and posting is async. Then a 280-character limit.
dc28.brief:
Simmer is a recipe site. App.tsx loads the comments (already done) and renders CommentItem with its ReplyItems. Each comment has a Reply link that does nothing yet.

A teammate already built ReplyBox in App.tsx (textarea, Cancel, Post reply; it owns its draft and calls onSubmit(text)), but nothing renders it. Read api.ts: postReply(commentId, text) resolves after a random 0.7–1.2 s with the new Reply. components/Avatar.tsx and utils/time.ts are worth reusing.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (5 is a stretch). Change (~16 min): a 280-character limit.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–16 Core · 16–20 change · 20–25 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Only one reply box can be open, so CommentSection stores replyingTo: string | null, the id of the comment, not a boolean per comment. Each CommentItem gets replying and renders the existing ReplyBox under itself. On submit the section calls postReply; when it resolves, it adds the reply into that comment's replies with a nested map + spread and sets replyingTo to null, which unmounts the box. Then ReplyBox gets a pending flag so it can't post twice."
requirements: Clicking Reply opens the existing <ReplyBox /> under that comment only. Clicking Reply on another comment moves the box there. Cancel closes it

Post reply calls postReply(commentId, text). When it resolves, the reply appears at the end of that comment's replies (author "You", "just now") and the box closes. State is updated immutably (nested map + spread)
While pending the button reads Posting… and the textarea and both buttons are disabled. Post reply is disabled while the text is blank
The textarea is focused when the box opens and its placeholder reads "Reply to Nadia Q.…" (pass the author in)

Replies start collapsed. Under a comment with replies, a muted link reads Show 3 replies (or Show 1 reply); clicking shows them and it becomes Hide replies. No link without replies. After you post a reply, that thread is expanded

change.title: 280-character limit
change.html:
"Moderation wants replies short."

  • Replies are capped at 280 characters. Left of Cancel, a muted counter reads 280 left and counts down as you type.
  • Past the limit it goes negative (-5 left), turns red and bold, and Post reply is disabled.

It's derived from the text: no new state.

hints: How many reply boxes can be open at once? One. So store which comment, not a flag per comment: useState<string | null>(null).
In the map: const replying = replyingTo === c.id; then CommentItem renders <ReplyBox /> only when replying.
Nested update: prev.map((c) => { if (c.id !== commentId) { return c; } return { ...c, replies: [...c.replies, reply] }; })
Search: "react async form submit loading state". Set pending to true before calling onSubmit; the box unmounts on success, so you don't need to set it back.
Counter: const left = 280 - text.length; inside ReplyBox, a class built above (char-count / char-count is-over), and add left < 0 to the disabled condition.
Collapse (stretch): const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({}); and toggle with setExpanded((prev) => { return { ...prev, [id]: !prev[id] }; });
rubric: replyingTo stores one id; only one box possible
Reused ReplyBox; section owns the data, box owns the draft
Nested immutable update (map + spread twice)
Pending state disables input and changes the label
Counter derived from text (no new state); disabled over the limit
Stretch: collapse state keyed by id, label pluralised, expands after posting

primitives.note: Store the id of the open item instead of a boolean per item. Opening another one automatically closes the first.

primitives.note: Copy each level you change: a new comment object and a new replies array. Pushing into c.replies would mutate state.

<ReplyBox onSubmit={(text) => { onPostReply(comment.id, text); }} />

dc29.title: Travel listing: photo carousel
dc29.summary: A vacation rental page shows one photo. Make it a carousel: wrapping prev/next, dots, a counter, and autoplay that pauses on hover.
dc29.brief:
Wanderstay is a vacation rental site. App.tsx loads the listing (already done) and renders Gallery, which only shows the first photo, plus details and a BookingCard.

Read components/PhotoSlide.tsx: it renders any photo. Reuse it for the current slide. There are 7 photos.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change (~19 min): keyboard arrows.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan · 5–19 Core · 19–23 change · 23–28 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Gallery owns index and paused. Next is (i + 1) % count, prev is (i - 1 + count) % count so it wraps both ways. Autoplay is an effect with setInterval that skips when paused and clears in the cleanup. I'll put index in its deps so a manual click restarts the 4 s countdown. Hover sets paused with onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave. The counter is derived: index + 1 of count."
requirements: Round ‹ / › buttons on the photo go to the previous / next photo, wrapping (next on 7 goes to 1, prev on 1 goes to 7)
A row of dots at the bottom (active one white and larger); clicking a dot jumps to that photo. A pill at the bottom right reads 3 / 7
Autoplay advances every 4 s. It pauses while the mouse is over the carousel and resumes on leave. The interval is cleared on unmount and never doubles up
A manual move restarts the 4 s countdown (no jump right after a click)

change.title: Keyboard arrows
change.html:
"Accessibility review: the carousel can't be used without a mouse."

  • The carousel is focusable (tabIndex={0}, visible focus ring) with role="region" and aria-label="Listing photos".
  • While it has focus, ArrowLeft / ArrowRight go prev / next (same wrapping).
  • Arrow keys elsewhere on the page do nothing to it.

hints: Wrapping is modulo. Going back: add count before % so it never goes negative.
Search: "react setInterval useEffect cleanup". Return early when paused; the cleanup clears the interval.
Inside the interval use the updater: setIndex((i) => { return (i + 1) % count; });
Search: "mdn mouseenter vs mouseover". onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave don't fire again for children.
Search: "mdn tabindex" and "react onKeyDown". Put onKeyDown on the focusable carousel div, not on document.
rubric: Index-only state; counter and active dot derived
Correct wrap both directions
Interval in an effect with cleanup; pause state respected
Reused PhotoSlide
Keyboard handled on the focusable element, not globally
ARIA labels on icon buttons and dots

dc30.title: Coffee shop: cart drawer
dc30.summary: Add a cart to a coffee-gear store: add from the catalog, list it in the (scaffolded) drawer with a subtotal, then quantities, totals and a coupon.
dc30.brief:
Ember & Oak sells pour-over gear. App.tsx loads the products (done) and renders ProductCards with an Add to cart button that does nothing, and a Cart button (badge stuck at 0) that opens components/CartDrawer.tsx. A teammate scaffolded that drawer on the shared Drawer shell (backdrop, ✕), but it always says "Your cart is empty."

Read these first: utils/money.ts (all prices are integer cents; formatMoney, calcTax (8.25%) and percentOf), utils/cart.ts (CartLine and joinCart, which attaches each product to its line) and components/LineItem.tsx (one row: image, name, any children, line total). In api.ts, validateCoupon(code) takes 0.5–1.0 s and only accepts SAVE10 (any case).

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (5 is a stretch). Change (~21 min): free-shipping progress bar.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan · 6–21 Core · 21–26 change · 26–30 Next + talk

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The cart is { productId, qty }[] in App, because the header badge and the drawer both need it. I don't copy names or prices into the cart; the drawer uses joinCart to attach products. The badge count and the subtotal are derived with reduce on every render, in cents, and only formatted at the end. Then quantity and remove are two more updaters in App passed down, tax and total are more derived numbers, and if there's time the coupon lives in App too, so it survives closing the drawer."
requirements: Add to cart adds one of that product (adding again increases its quantity). The cart is { productId, qty }[] in App. The header badge shows the total item count
The drawer lists each line with the existing <LineItem /> (use joinCart) and a Subtotal row under it with formatMoney: 2 × Ceramic dripper shows $56.00 on the line and as the subtotal
Each line has − qty + (− disabled at 1) and Remove; removing the last line shows "Your cart is empty."
Under Subtotal: Tax (8.25%) using calcTax and Total, plus a Checkout button. 2 × Ceramic dripper: tax $4.62, total $60.62

A coupon field + Apply calls validateCoupon (button reads "Checking…" meanwhile). Invalid: red Code "BOGUS" isn't valid. SAVE10: a green "SAVE10 applied · 10% off" with Remove, and a Discount row; tax is on the discounted subtotal. The coupon survives closing and reopening the drawer

change.title: Free-shipping progress bar
change.html:
"Marketing wants to nudge order size. Free shipping starts at $75."

  • At the top of the drawer: Add $19.00 more for free shipping with a progress bar (amber fill) showing subtotal / $75.
  • At $75 or more: You've unlocked free shipping, green background, full green bar.
  • Use the subtotal before the discount.

It's all derived: no new state.

hints: What does the cart need to remember? Only which product and how many. Price and name come from the product list (joinCart does the lookup).
Add: find the line. If it exists, map it to { ...line, qty: line.qty + 1 }; otherwise [...prev, { productId, qty: 1 }].
Badge: cart.reduce((sum, line) => { return sum + line.qty; }, 0). Subtotal: lines.reduce((sum, l) => { return sum + l.product.price * l.qty; }, 0).
Search: "javascript floating point money cents". That's why everything is integer cents until formatMoney. Tax: calcTax(subtotal - discount).
Coupon form: setChecking(true); validateCoupon(code).then((result) => { setChecking(false); if (result.ok) { onApply(...); } else { setError(result.message); } });
Progress: const percent = Math.min(100, Math.round((subtotal / 7500) * 100)); then style={{ width: percent + "%" }}.
rubric: Cart stores ids + qty in App; reused joinCart and LineItem for display
All money math in cents with the existing helpers
Count, subtotal, tax, total derived, never stored
Immutable add / change qty / remove
Progress bar derived, no new state
Stretch: coupon has pending, error and success states and lives in App

primitives.name: reduce() to sum
primitives.example: [{ qty: 2 }, { qty: 1 }].reduce((sum, l) => { return sum + l.qty; }, 0)   // 3
primitives.note: Walks the array carrying a running value; returns the final value. Always pass the start value (0), or an empty array throws.

primitives.name: find()
primitives.example: cart.find((l) => { return l.productId === 'p2'; })   // the line, or undefined
primitives.note: Returns the first item that matches, or undefined. Use it to ask "is this product already in the cart?".

primitives.name: Money in integer cents
primitives.note: Decimals are inexact in JS. Keep money as whole cents and only divide + toFixed(2) (a string) when displaying.

primitives.name: Math.min to clamp
